name: cpu_cad_solver

license.notes: Task source and the bundled bracket model (assets/bracket.mesh, generated by tools/gen_model.py) stay source-available; AMGCL is MIT and the LLVM OpenMP runtime is Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, neither imposes copyleft. gmsh (GPL) is only used offline to generate the mesh and is not part of the task.

libraries.name: AMGCL
libraries.usage: Builds the smoothed aggregation algebraic multigrid preconditioner (3x3 node blocks, ILU(0) smoothing) and runs the preconditioned conjugate gradient solve of every timed solve.
libraries.notes: Header only library compiled into the task from the pinned submodule with AMGCL_NO_BOOST; no source modifications. AMGCL is used in research and engineering codes for the linear systems of finite element and finite volume discretizations.

libraries.name: LLVM OpenMP runtime (libomp)
libraries.usage: Runs AMGCL's and the assembly's OpenMP parallel loops on macOS, where Apple clang ships no OpenMP runtime.
libraries.notes: Built as a static library from the pinned llvm-project submodule (openmp runtime only) and linked into macOS builds. Other platforms use the compiler's own OpenMP runtime (libgomp, vcomp or libomp), which is part of the toolchain like the C++ standard library.

title: Engineering simulation solver
short_description: Finite element stress analysis of a steel bracket across all cores.

structured_text.description: Runs a static stress analysis of a bundled steel mounting bracket the way engineering simulation tools do. Each solve assembles the stiffness matrix of a quadratic tetrahedral mesh with about 80,000 unknowns, builds an algebraic multigrid preconditioner and runs a conjugate gradient solver to a tight tolerance, all on every core. The model, loads and tolerances are fixed, and every result is checked against the reference solution, so scores compare directly between machines.
structured_text.metric_explanation: The score is the number of complete solves per minute, from assembly to the converged displacement field.
structured_text.value_interpretation: Higher is better. More solves per minute means faster design cycles, since engineers wait on these solves between every change.
structured_text.reasoning: Sparse solvers stress irregular memory access, memory bandwidth and double precision math in the pattern real CAD and engineering tools use. Algebraic multigrid preconditioned conjugate gradients is the standard iterative method for large structural models, so this reflects simulation performance far better than a clean throughput test.
